claims.text: HEA coating wear performance is primarily governed by formation of a uniform tribo-oxide layer.
An equiatomic elemental distribution enables formation of a uniform protective oxide film.
The protective oxide film forms in situ under sliding-wear conditions.
The tribo-oxide film is self-passivating or self-healing.
The oxide film reinforces the coating's hardness.
The oxide film reduces crack initiation and microcrack formation.
Suppression of cracking by the oxide film minimizes wear rate.
The baseline is a microwave-cladded Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20 coating on SS-304 steel.
The as-deposited baseline coating has a homogeneous microstructure.
Reducing Cu from 20 wt% to about 10 wt% while compensating with other elements disturbs the equiatomic balance.
A protective spinel oxide of the form (Fe,Co,Ni,Mn,Cu)3O4 can form in the Fe-Co-Ni-Mn-Cu coating system.
The (Fe,Co,Ni,Mn,Cu)3O4 protective phase forms specifically during sliding wear.
An even elemental distribution produces a lattice-distortion strengthening effect.
Balanced elemental fractions promote homogeneous nucleation and growth of the protective oxide during wear.
Reducing Cu causes uneven oxide formation and compromises the protective barrier.
The Cu-reduced coating will have a higher wear rate than the equiatomic baseline.
The equiatomic coating will have relatively stable friction, whereas the Cu-reduced coating will show more variable friction because of oxide inhomogeneity and microcracking.
The baseline coating has a wear rate around 0.0018 mm3/m and a friction coefficient close to 0.2 under the specified test conditions.
The proposed mechanism should hold in ambient or moderately high-temperature sliding conditions where tribo-oxidation is significant.
Phase segregation and processing parameters can affect oxide-layer uniformity.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as equiatomic Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20, which ordinarily denotes equal atomic fractions, but the intervention treats its Cu level as 20 wt%. Equal atomic and equal weight fractions are not equivalent for these elements, so the composition basis is internally inconsistent.
